chapters.title: 1. Introduction
chapters.summary: Motivation and contributions: effects should be visible in types and inferred automatically, using row polymorphism with duplicate labels, with a semantic (not merely syntactic) meaning.

chapters.title: 2. Overview
chapters.summary: A tour of the language: effect-annotated function types, the basic effects and their aliases, polymorphic effects in higher-order functions, why duplicate labels help, heap effects and their encapsulation, safe state with let-polymorphism, divergence, and experience writing real programs.

chapters.title: 3. The type system
chapters.summary: The formal system: kinds for values, effect rows, effect constants and heaps; effect equivalence up to reordering; and the declarative typing rules, including run and catch.

chapters.title: 4. Semantics of effects
chapters.summary: Operational semantics with explicit heap binders: values and answers, reduction rules for exceptions, references and run, and evaluation contexts for strict evaluation.

chapters.title: 5. Semantic soundness
chapters.summary: Type soundness in the Wright–Felleisen style: subject reduction (with a lemma that state cannot be silently discarded) and the absence of faulty expressions, including escaping references.

chapters.title: 6. Effectful semantics
chapters.summary: Theorems giving effects semantic meaning: without exn there are no uncaught exceptions, without st no observable heap, and without div evaluation terminates (via a logical relation).

chapters.title: 7. Related work
chapters.summary: Comparison with earlier effect systems, monadic approaches, region inference and Lindley–Cheney’s row-based effects.

chapters.title: Appendix A. Type inference
chapters.summary: The inference algorithm: a syntax-directed system, algorithmic rules, and unification for types and effect rows, sound and complete with respect to the declarative rules.

title: Koka: Programming with Row-polymorphic Effect Types
note: PDF page N is printed page N+99. References (PDF pp. 22–24) are not broken out. This paper predates Koka’s algebraic effect handlers: effects here are built-in (exn, div, st), and handlers arrive in Leijen’s later papers. Summaries are in our own words; the text stays in the PDF.
summary: An ML-like language whose function types carry an inferred effect row, so total, partial, divergent and stateful code are told apart by type. The key design choice is row polymorphism with duplicate labels: effect rows are equal up to reordering but ⟨exn, exn⟩ is not ⟨exn⟩, which keeps Hindley–Milner inference principal without lacks constraints or presence flags and gives catch a natural type. The paper gives the type system, a reduction semantics with scoped heaps, and soundness proofs showing the effects mean something: no exn means no uncaught exceptions, no div means termination, and run safely encapsulates local state (like runST) while making the ML value restriction unnecessary.
